chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who married a young girl who had not yet reached puberty, whom he would not have intercourse with like an adult, or who married a virgin (ratqa') and she was brought to him, and he divorced her immediately after she was brought to him. He said: In these two cases, a trustworthy woman is sent to examine them. If they are as they entered (i.e., virgins), she is entitled to half of the dowry he specified for her, and there is no waiting period (iddah) for her from him. He said: And if the husband dies regarding them before divorcing them, then she is entitled to the inheritance and half of the dowry, and upon them is the waiting period of four months and ten days.

key_terms.رَتْقَاءَ: a virgin (one whose hymen is intact)

ai.seo_question: What is the dowry and waiting period for a wife if the husband divorces her before consummating the marriage with a young girl or virgin?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir) via Zurarah, emphasizing the role of trustworthy female witnesses in verifying virginity to determine the dowry share. This hadith clarifies the distinction between partial and full consumption of marriage, ensuring that a woman who has not yet been intimate with her husband receives only half the mahr upon divorce, while retaining inheritance rights if the husband dies before consummation.
